CPS_s1.explanation: The unit responds to upright canine faces, firing most on the eye region of dogs, wolves and foxes seen from the front. It gives weaker responses to other upright furry mammal faces (red panda, bear) and very weak ones to human or bird faces.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to upright canine faces, firing most on the eye region of dogs, wolves and foxes seen from the front. It gives weaker responses to other upright furry mammal faces (red panda, bear) and very weak ones to human or bird faces.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top photos are dog, wolf or fox faces boxed near the eye, and the one random dog photo scores 8 while non-canine random photos score 0-3. The unit is very sensitive to rotate_180 (percentile 0), patch shuffle (1) and edge map (4), which fits a configural, upright, texture-dependent face detector, and the lower ranges drift to red panda (7), then bear, human and rooster (2-4).
parsed.missing_data: Activations on other mammal faces such as cats and bears, and on dog photos where the face is hidden, to tell whether the unit is specific to canines or responds to animal faces in general.

CPS_s2.explanation: The unit responds to upright, front-facing canid faces (dogs, wolves, foxes), peaking around the eye region between the eye and the ear or forehead. It also responds more weakly to similar faces of other furry mammals, such as a red panda, a bear and people.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to upright, front-facing canid faces (dogs, wolves, foxes), peaking around the eye region between the eye and the ear or forehead. It also responds more weakly to similar faces of other furry mammals, such as a red panda, a bear and people.
parsed.evidence: All top-20 photos are dog, wolf or fox faces with the box on the eye area, and the only high random photo is a dog face (activation 8). Lower ranges move to a red panda (7), a human face (4) and a bear (2), and the unit loses far more than most units under rotate_180, patch shuffling and edge maps, which fits a configural, upright face detector that depends on fur texture and shading.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on non-canid animal faces such as cats and other mammals in quantity, plus crops of just the eye region versus the whole face, to separate a canid-face detector from a general furry-face or eye detector.

CPSN_s3.explanation: The unit responds to the upright, front-facing face of a canid (dog, wolf, fox), peaking at the eye/upper-cheek region of a frontal dog face. It responds more weakly to other frontal mammal-like faces such as a red panda, a bear and a human cheek.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the upright, front-facing face of a canid (dog, wolf, fox), peaking at the eye/upper-cheek region of a frontal dog face. It responds more weakly to other frontal mammal-like faces such as a red panda, a bear and a human cheek.
parsed.evidence: All top-20 crops are frontal dog, wolf or fox faces, and a random dog-face photo scores 8. Dogs seen from the side, from behind or too small (near misses) score near 0, and the unit is very sensitive to rotate_180 (percentile 0), patch_shuffle (1) and edge_map (4), which fits an upright, configured face detector.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on frontal cat or other non-canid mammal faces, plus inverted dog faces, would show how specific it is to canids versus faces in general.
